text:
Vegas arrives in Boston for game one of a four-game road trip with some repair work to do. The Golden Knights are 1-3-1 in their last five and were outscored 20-11 in that stretch, most recently a 5-2 home loss to New Jersey, and they're without Parker Wotherspoon. Boston is coming off a 5-4 overtime win over Chicago, where the Bruins erased a two-goal deficit and Elias Lindholm won it 2:32 into the extra period. It's also a homecoming for Vegas defenseman Noah Hanifin.

Our numbers see little separating them. At five on five, Vegas has taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and Boston 52%, and our model projects 3.13 goals for VGK and 2.88 for BOS. Boston's results run ahead of its chances, with finishing and goaltending doing the lifting. The Bruins also take 4.8 penalties a game, and their penalty kill allows 0.68 expected goals per game against Vegas's 0.39. In net, projected starter Carter Hart sits at -0.7 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops beyond what the shots should produce) this season and -4.4 last year. Jeremy Swayman is at +6.6 and +26.5.

Jack Eichel is our top pick for two or more points for Vegas at 35%. Mitch Marner carries a nine-game point streak, and as Jesse Granger of The Athletic posted, he "dished it against the grain to Barbashev for a tap in." David Pastrnak is Boston's best bet to score at 33%, and Morgan Geekie tied Friday's game with 10 seconds left, per Jon Lane of NHL.com.
